title: Condensed exceptional inverse image of a reconstructed finite-level system
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive prime characteristic different from $\ell$, and a $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. On a scheme $T$ equal to $X$ or $Y$, write $\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,T}=\varprojlim_n (\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_T$, and let $\mathcal I_T$ be the completed integral constructible category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z_\ell$. Its rationalization has morphisms $\operatorname{Hom}(L,M)\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Let $J_T:\mathcal I_T[1/\ell]\simeq\mathcal C^c_E(T)$ be the scalar-extension realization of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization]. Let $E_T^c=p_T^*C(-,\mathbf Q_\ell)$ and $\Omega_T^c=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, where $\underline\Omega(S)$ consists of continuous maps on the profinite set $S$ with values in one finite intermediate field of $\Omega/E$, as in [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category, prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. Define the functor
$$U_T:\mathcal I_T\longrightarrow\mathcal C^c_\Omega(T),\qquad U_T(L)=\Omega_T^c\otimes^L_{E_T^c}J_T(L[1/\ell]).$$

For $L\in\mathcal I_Y$ put $L_n=L\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,Y}}(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_Y$. Let $Rf_n^!$ denote the constructible exceptional inverse image obtained from the ordinary etale compact-support right adjoint by site comparison, as explicitly constructed for arbitrary $k$ in [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons]. Suppose supplied a strict semilinear derived tower $M_\bullet\in D(\mathscr S_X)$, where $\mathscr S_X$ is the abelian coefficient-system category of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], and use its underlying completed-coefficient tower in taking $R\varprojlim$. It has specified level identifications $\phi_n:M_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_n^!L_n$, normalization isomorphisms $M_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1,X}}A_{n,X}\simeq M_n$, transitions induced by these isomorphisms and the quotient maps, and the quotient cocycle, where $A_{n,T}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_T$. Require that the $\phi_n$ intertwine these transitions with the exceptional-image quotient transitions. In addition require either (a) the $\phi_n$ are the evaluations of a specified identification of normalized derived systems with the exceptional section $G(\mathcal R_YL)$ of [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates, lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons], or (b) there is one integer $r$ such that every $M_n$ has cohomology only in degree $r$. In case (b) no enhanced identification or section counit is additional input: the comparison is defined by the functorial good-truncation identification of each system with its degree-$r$ cohomology diagram, and the strict isomorphism of cohomology diagrams induced by the $\phi_n$. In either case the section counit is the geometric section counit transported through that identification. Suppose each cohomology sheaf of each level is constructible in the intrinsic finite-stratification sense of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], and the levels have a common finite cohomological interval independent of $n$. Assume $M=R\varprojlim M_\bullet$ lies in $\mathcal I_X$, with its canonical reductions identified with $M_n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Then there is a natural isomorphism
$$c_{f,L,M_\bullet}:U_X(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,\Omega}^{\,R}(U_YL).$$
Here $Rf_{!,\Omega}$ is the bounded constructible condensed-module compact-support functor, defined using extension by zero and proper direct image in the chosen Nagata compactification, and $Rf_{!,\Omega}^{\,R}$ is its chosen right adjoint on $\mathcal C^c_\Omega$, namely $\mathrm{boundedConstructibleUpperShriek}(\mathrm{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell),\ell,f)$ at master commit 7347520d9b0d17cc31d0fc34ea20f1381a83fe13. More explicitly, fix the chosen compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{g}Y$ and a right adjoint of its bounded constructible proper direct image $Rg_{*,\Omega}$, as required by the master declaration's left-adjoint instance. Then this right adjoint is $(Rg_{*,\Omega})^R$ followed by $j^*$, with the adjunction obtained by composing $j_!\dashv j^*$ and the chosen $Rg_{*,\Omega}\dashv(Rg_{*,\Omega})^R$. This assertion concerns this constructible right adjoint and asserts no unbounded ambient pro-etale adjoint. The isomorphism is the adjunction comparison: its counit is induced by the finite-level exceptional counits under completed reconstruction, localization and extension to $\Omega$. It is compatible with a refinement of the compactification and with morphisms of the supplied coherent systems. Here such a morphism consists of a map of integral inputs and an actual derived-system map commuting with the identifications with the geometric exceptional sections. In case (b), for two data sets concentrated in the same degree r, commutation of the level-identification squares suffices for this system compatibility, because maps between degree-r cohomology diagrams are determined componentwise. In addition $U_T$ sends the integral coefficient object to the condensed tensor unit and commutes with shifts.

source.place: Agent-formulated comparison obligation for the exact master functors: boundedConstructibleUpperShriekOfCompactification (lines 100–118), boundedConstructibleUpperShriek and its adjunction (lines 128–146), commit 7347520d9b0d17cc31d0fc34ea20f1381a83fe13. proof.text: Work first over a finite coefficient field E, initially Q_ell, and write R=O_E, t=varpi_E. The schemes X,Y are qcqs and locally noetherian, hence noetherian (a qc scheme has a finite subcover of its noetherian affine cover), and have finite dimension. The prime ell is invertible because the base has characteristic p different from ell. The stratified-perfect characterization applies to every integral object K: on each of finitely many strata it is locally Rhat tensor_R a bounded finite-projective R-complex. Each stratum is quasi-compact, and the pro-etale covering condition lets us select finitely many affine covering pieces from its local perfect descriptions. Tensoring each of their bounded projective representatives with R/t^n gives a common finite Tor interval for all K_n: take the minimum and maximum degrees over these finitely many representatives on finitely many strata. Here is the detection argument for an arbitrary degree-zero coefficient-module sheaf N. Exact inverse image for constant coefficients and the derived tensor-pullback comparison identify the restriction of K_n tensor^L N with the tensor of the two restrictions. The covering-family criterion detects its cohomology vanishing on each stratum from the displayed bounded projective models. To pass from strata to the scheme, write each locally closed stratum as C minus D for closed subsets D contained in C. Successively split along the finitely many such closed subsets and their open complements. Every final piece lies in a stratum. At each split, the ringed open-closed short exact sequence says a cohomology sheaf is zero when both its restrictions are zero; reverse the finite sequence of splits. Thus the same Tor interval works on the whole scheme for every N. This uses covering and open-closed detection, without claiming conservativity of ordinary pro-etale geometric stalks. In particular L_n, M_n (using the assumed M in I_X and its reductions), and all test reductions used below belong to the finite-Tor constructible categories. No finite-Tor assertion is inferred merely from constructibility.

proof.text: For A_n=R/t^n, take the enhanced finite categories C_n=D^b_ctf(X,A_n), D_n=D^b_ctf(Y,A_n). The finite geometric comparison lemma gives F_n=Rf_!,n, its right adjoint G_n=Rf_n^!, the coherent equivalences q for reduction, and invertible mates b defined by the counit formula in that lemma. The semilinear section theorem supplies simultaneous enhanced models for open extension, proper pushforward and q. The cartesian-section adjoint-mate theorem therefore applies: F and G act on normalized sections, the exceptional section is G(R_Y L), and H_Y(F R_X K,R_Y L) is isomorphic to H_X(R_X K,G R_Y L) as a derived inverse system of mapping complexes, with the specified counit and all composition coherences. Write N_bullet=G(R_Y L) in D(S_X), with its actual geometric section counit. The next step constructs the required identification with M_bullet under either alternative in the statement.

source.place: 6.7.18 finite coefficient adjunction and reduction; enhanced section assembly by the cited generic tools

proof.text: Identify M_bullet with N_bullet before taking a limit. In case (a) use the supplied identification. In case (b), exact evaluation in the semilinear abelian category computes cohomology componentwise, so both systems have cohomology only in degree r, since their levels are identified by phi_n. Apply good truncations in this abelian category to a strict representative C of either system: the natural zigzag C ← tau_le_r C → H^r(C)[-r] consists of componentwise quasi-isomorphisms. The left arrow is inclusion, and the right arrow is quotient of ker(d^r) by im(d^(r-1)) in degree r and zero in lower degrees. Thus it defines a natural identification in D(S_X). Applying H^r to the commuting transition squares for phi_n gives an actual isomorphism of sheaf diagrams H^r(M_bullet)→H^r(N_bullet) in S_X, since restriction of coefficients is exact. Conjugate its single-complex map by these truncation zigzags to obtain theta:M_bullet→N_bullet. Naturality of the same truncations in each level derived category shows ev_n(theta)=phi_n, including their normalization adjoints. Its inverse is obtained from the inverse sheaf-diagram map. For two systems concentrated in the same degree r, the full subcategory of D(S_X) concentrated in that degree is identified by H^r with the abelian category S_X: the displayed zigzags identify every map with its cohomology-diagram map. A commuting square of the level identifications is therefore a commuting square in S_X and then in D(S_X). This proves naturality for these morphisms and for compactification comparisons. For general enhanced data the morphisms are required to commute with the supplied section identifications, as specified in the statement; no claim that evaluations detect equality of arbitrary derived-system maps is used. Transport the already constructed section counit through theta; this supplies its higher coherence without lifting an arbitrary homotopy-category transformation. This alternative applies to the immutable target parent: lem-pur-finite-smooth-adjunction-general-base says every exceptional image of the finite unit is concentrated in degree r=-2d, and its quotient compatibility is precisely the transition square required here. The parent explicitly uses the strict twist-sheaf tower in that degree. Hence its existing finite-unit data supply case (b), with no new hypothesis on the target.

proof.text:
Let K be any object of I_X(R), and let P_R be the compact-support reconstruction functor. Its comparison alpha identifies R_Y(P_R K) with F R_X K as normalized derived systems. Write L_T for the total-limit functor of the system evaluation calculus. That calculus, the preceding mapping-system adjunction and alpha give the natural chain
RHom_X(K,M) = RHom_X(K,L_X M_bullet) ≃ Rlim H_X(R_X K,M_bullet) ≃ Rlim H_Y(F R_X K,R_Y L) ≃ RHom_Y(P_R K,L_Y R_Y L) ≃ RHom_Y(P_R K,L).
The last arrow uses the actual derived-completeness isomorphism L→L_Y R_Y L in the definition of I_Y. These are isomorphisms of derived mapping complexes; take H^0 only after forming the displayed chain. This gives R-linear, natural inverse bijections Hom_X(K,M)≃Hom_Y(P_R K,L). The projection identities for gamma and the section adjunction show that the image of id_M is a morphism P_R M→L whose coherent reductions, conjugated by alpha and the supplied reduction identification, are exactly epsilon_n:F_n M_n→L_n. This is a statement about the specified derived-system map; equality is not deduced from equality of evaluations of arbitrary morphisms.

proof.text:
Tensor the R-linear inverse Hom bijections of Step 4 with E. The raw rationalized categories have precisely these tensor Hom groups, and exact linear functors and their transformations extend to them by h/t^r↦F(h)/t^r. Thus the same bijection holds on rationalized integral categories, with its same counit. Apply the E-linear equivalences J_X,J_Y and the compact-support comparison a. Every C in C_E^c(X) has a lattice by the realization theorem, so this yields, naturally in all C,
Hom_E(C,J_X(M[1/t])) ≃ Hom_E(P_E^c C,J_Y(L[1/t])).
This is the assertion that J_X M represents this Hom functor at the supplied L. No global integral right-adjoint preservation theorem over an algebraically closed finite field is being applied to k.

proof.text:
This representation is compatible with every finite extension E⊂F. Indeed, put S=O_F and form L_S and M_S by ordinary derived extension from Rhat to Shat. The finite-free completed-scalar comparison identifies this operation with completed integral scalar extension, and the constructibility theorem, together with the stratified-perfect characterization, puts both objects in I(S). Use the actual derived-system isomorphism theta constructed in Step 3. On the cofinal quotients S/t^nS=S/v^(en), apply enhanced coefficient extension to theta, then compose with the finite-free exceptional mate b. This is an actual map of enhanced systems, identifying the reductions of M_S with G_(S/t^nS) of the reductions of L_S. Its section counit is the scalar extension of the section counit, by the specified counit equation for b. The mixed quotient coherences of the finite geometric lemma extend this comparison to the finer v-adic quotient diagram. In particular this supplies case (a) over F; a nonflat further quotient need not preserve the single-degree condition of case (b). At every m, associativity identifies (M tensor_Rhat Shat) tensor_Shat (S/v^m) with M tensor_Rhat (S/v^m), and the quotient-induced maps commute with this balancing identification; the same holds for L. For any m choose n with en at least m. Reduce the finite-free identification at S/v^(en) further to S/v^m, and compose with the S/v^(en) to S/v^m exceptional mate. The quotient cocycle and mixed coefficient coherences of the finite geometric lemma make this independent of n and compatible as m varies, including the counits. The completed-scalar comparison identifies the resulting total limits with M_S and L_S. Thus the hypotheses of Steps 2–5 hold over F. Tensor associativity in the definition of J identifies J_F((M_S)[1/v]) with T_EF J_E(M[1/t]), and similarly for L. Hence for every C_F in C_F^c(X) there are natural inverse bijections
Hom_F(C_F,T_EF J_E M) ≃ Hom_F(P_F^c C_F,T_EF J_E L).
The specified finite coefficient counit identities, the compact-support comparison with scalar extension, and tensor associativity make these bijections compatible with further finite extensions, identities and their composition coherences. In particular this claim is about every F-stage test object, not just scalar extensions of E-stage objects.

proof.text:
Return to E=Q_ell. An arbitrary C in C_Omega^c(X) descends to some C_F at a finite F/E by the filtered two-colimit theorem. Each Hom from C to U_X M is the filtered colimit, over finite H containing F, of Hom_H(T_FH C_F,T_EH J_E M); this is precisely the morphism description in that theorem. Apply the compatible bijections of Step 6 at H. The compact-support scalar comparison identifies P_H T_FH C_F with T_FH P_F C_F, and identifies P_Omega C with T_FOmega P_F C_F. The resulting colimit on the other side is Hom_Omega(P_Omega C,U_Y L), by the same two-colimit theorem. The inverse maps commute with the transition maps as well, so their filtered colimits are inverse. Descent of morphisms and eventual equality give naturality independently of the chosen finite field and descended object. We have therefore constructed
Hom_Omega(C,U_X M) ≃ Hom_Omega(P_Omega C,U_Y L)
for every C, with counit t:P_Omega U_X M→U_Y L obtained from the finite-stage counits. This argument uses the finite-extension-valued Omega coefficient ring, not the full ring of all continuous Omega-valued functions.

source.place: 6.8 finite-field descent, with the explicit archived condensed coefficient two-colimit

proof.text: Let R be the exact chosen bounded-constructible right adjoint of P_Omega specified in the statement and the archived master, and let epsilon^R be its counit. Define c:U_X M→R(U_Y L) to be the adjoint transpose of t. For every C, postcomposition by c is the Step 7 representation followed by the chosen adjunction bijection, hence is bijective. In particular choose r:R(U_Y L)→U_X M mapping to id_R; then c r=id_R. Injectivity with C=U_X M implies r c=id, so c is an isomorphism and epsilon^R∘P_Omega(c)=t. For a map of supplied coherent systems, naturality of the representation implies the corresponding square for c, since both composites have the same adjoint transpose. For a compactification refinement write q:P^1→P^2 for its compact-support comparison and R^1,R^2 for the chosen right adjoints. Define rho:R^2→R^1 by transposing epsilon^2 composed with q_(R^2); transposing q inverse gives its inverse, by the two adjunction triangle identities. The finite geometric counit and compact-support refinement coherences in Steps 2–7 give t^1=t^2 composed with q_(U_X M). The two maps c^1 and rho composed with c^2 therefore have this same transpose, and are equal. This is the required refinement square. This proves compatibility of the specified comparison, rather than merely abstract isomorphism of the two objects.

proof.text: Finally J_T is derived extension from the completed integral ring, so it takes that ring to E_T^c: multiplication gives B tensor_A A≃B with inverse b↦b tensor 1. Extending once more to Omega gives U_T(Rhat_T)≃Omega_T^c, the condensed tensor unit. J_T and derived coefficient extension commute with shifts; the latter is explicitly computed by exact termwise tensor. Their composite U_T therefore commutes with shifts, with the usual coherent shift identifications.
